title: Cypress Examples
description: Small Cypress examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Meet the Cypress runner
examples.description: Cypress runs browser checks as a chain of commands. This example starts with a blank local practice page.

examples.title: Select a clear target
examples.description: A stable data attribute can identify a control without tying a test to its visual style.

examples.title: Type into a field
examples.description: type enters text and clear removes existing text. A final value check confirms the input received it.

examples.title: Click and check the effect
examples.description: A click test needs an observable result. Here the button changes its own text.

examples.title: Retry an assertion
examples.description: Cypress retries many queries and assertions until they pass or time out. Check a real condition instead of guessing a delay.

examples.title: Read a yielded value
examples.description: then receives the value yielded by the previous command. This is how you inspect queued results.

examples.title: Work with checkboxes
examples.description: check requests the checked state. It states intent more clearly than a toggle click.

examples.title: Select a dropdown value
examples.description: select chooses a native option by value or text. Assert the stored value after the action.

examples.title: Count a collection
examples.description: A query can find several elements. have.length checks how many the query found.

examples.title: Intercept a request
examples.description: intercept can supply a known network response. Set it up before the page sends the request.

examples.title: Keep tests independent
examples.description: A test should set up the state it needs. Cypress test isolation helps avoid state leaking from a previous test.

examples.title: Review failures and screenshots
examples.description: A failed assertion tells you which expected condition was not met. Use the command log and screenshot to understand it.
